elements.content: Grammar focus: Modifying Comparatives.

Judge the gap, then pick the modifier: much or far for a large one, slightly or marginally for a small one, no for none. Keep the comparative form intact after the modifier: much more expensive, not much expensive.

much / far — large difference: much faster, far more expensive
considerably / significantly — large, formal: considerably higher
slightly / marginally — small difference: slightly clearer
a bit / a little — small, informal: a bit cheaper
no / not any — no difference: no better, not any worse
even — surprising extra degree: even faster than expected
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'This option is ___ cheaper.'
2. Complete: 'The results are ___ better than last year.'
3. Which sentence is correct?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

much faster — a large difference (The new system is much faster.)
slightly clearer — a small difference (This draft is slightly clearer.)
no better — no difference at all (The second offer is no better.)
What do you observe?

A comparative can be graded by the size of the gap. Large: much, far, considerably, significantly, a great deal. Small: slightly, a little, a bit, marginally. None: no, not any. The modifier goes before the comparative adjective or adverb, and much and far work with both short and long forms.
1. Which modifier means there is no difference?
2. Which pair marks a large difference?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can debate which skills matter more.

Success criteria:
- I can grade a large difference with much and far.
- I can grade a small difference with slightly.
- I can say there is no difference with no.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ The new system is very faster (very with a comparative) → ✅ The new system is much faster
❌ This draft is slightly more clear (double comparative form) → ✅ This draft is slightly clearer
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The second version is significantly cheaper to run.
Response times are marginally slower.
The revised offer is no more attractive than the first.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where modifying comparatives carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
